correctness.rationale: Every Heawood perfect matching is among 7! possible line permutations. The incidence property yields a complete 24-item census and exact adjacency iff three point partners change; two independent exhaustive algorithms agree on 84 edges, all 24 BFS distance layers and every intersection number. The 24-vertex unique Klein graph with this array is a cited 1989 theorem, with its use explicitly scoped.

value.rationale: Reconfiguration by the shortest possible alternating cycle is a canonical matching dynamic on the smallest cubic girth-six graph. The resulting global topology is unexpectedly the Klein 24-vertex distance-regular graph, not merely a routine count; the complete three-move metric and antipodal three-cover distinguish the claim from established enumerations and abstract graph tables.
